title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and translation vector also set to zero. Draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. Begin by drawing the first loop with four lines: the first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0); the second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0084); the third line starts at (0.75, 0.0084) and ends at (0.0, 0.0084); the fourth line starts at (0.0, 0.0084) and returns to the origin. Apply a scaling factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translating it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Finally, extrude the sketch along the normal direction by 0.0419 units to create a solid body. The resulting dimensions are a length of 0.7500000000000001 units, a width of 0.008377017930541492 units, and a height of 0.04188508965270746 units.

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.0419)

# Assign the final model to 'r'

lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0084, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0084, 0.0419) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0419) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
